hardware: Intel Core i7-12700H, 16 GB RAM, Windows 11; NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU, 610.91, 6144 MiB; plugged in, OMEN performance mode, Windows best performance, lid open

proposals.statement: The client's current system has a paper diary that receptionists use to manage appointments, which leads to missed calls and double bookings

evidence.quote: All three clinics, Centurion, Irene and Olievenhoutbosch, have their own landline and their own paper diary at reception. The receptionist finds a gap, writes the pet's name and the owner's number in pencil, and that's it.

Mornings are the worst. Between eight and ten the phones just don't stop, and there's one receptionist per clinic who is also checking people in and taking payments. We miss a lot of calls. And people get double-booked, because someone rubbed out a booking and someone else wrote over it.

proposals.statement: The client wants to reduce missed calls, double bookings, and no-shows by implementing a new online booking system

evidence.quote: If I had to pick one, it's the phones. My receptionists are burning out.

proposals.statement: The new system should allow pet owners to book appointments online via a website on their phone, select a clinic and service type, and receive a reminder the day before

evidence.quote: They go onto a website on their phone, pick the clinic, pick what it's for, a vaccination, a check-up, a sick pet, and see the open times. They choose one and it's booked. And then they get a reminder the day before.

proposals.statement: The new system should automatically send vaccination reminders with a link to book appointments

evidence.quote: VetDesk knows when each animal is due. Right now Charmaine prints a list every month and the girls phone people. If that could go out automatically with a link to book, that's half the work gone.

proposals.statement: The new system should allow receptionists to view the day's appointments, move bookings around, and handle phone bookings for clients who prefer not to book online

evidence.quote: They need to see the day for their clinic, move bookings around, and put in phone bookings too, because some of our older clients will never book online.

proposals.statement: The system must only show bookings and reminders, not medical history

evidence.quote: No. Definitely not, not in this project. The vets don't want owners reading clinical notes without someone explaining them. Bookings and reminders only.

proposals.statement: VetDesk is an existing system with an API that can share data, but it charges per clinic and takes three months to switch on

evidence.quote: There is an API. Our rep mentioned it at a conference.
But they charge for it per clinic, and when the Pretoria East practice asked for it, it took VetDesk three months to switch it on.

proposals.statement: The system must run under two and a half thousand rand per month for all three clinics

evidence.quote: the running costs, the messages and the hosting, must stay under two and a half thousand a month for all three clinics. That's my limit.

proposals.statement: The client has allocated one hundred and eighty thousand rand for the project

evidence.quote: We've put aside a hundred and eighty thousand rand to build it.

proposals.statement: The system should use the client's green color, have big buttons, and be a simple web page without an app download

evidence.quote: Our green, the logo green. Big buttons, because half the people booking are holding a puppy in the other hand. And no app to download, just a web page.

proposals.statement: The system must be live by the first of February to handle vaccination season

evidence.quote: Before vaccination season. So live by the first of February at the latest.
Ideally mid-January, so the girls have two weeks to get used to it before the rush.

proposals.statement: The client wants to add pet food ordering and payment in the next year

evidence.quote: Ordering pet food online and paying for it, maybe. Next year.
